scope: Classify original 400-pixel crop RGB using exactly the saved RGB palette; compare to interpolation of the existing 256-pixel full-photo material probabilities. No new crop, palette fit, curve fit or acceptance rule.

existingWeaveReScore.scope: Re-score existing weave only, no new fit or geometry check; target differs from original experiment.

features.method: Both colours in the observed region; free pixels split components and do not enter their area or retention. At least 60% of each substantial weighted region with a solid core must remain its original colour. Regions touching the square border or its one-pixel neighbourhood are excluded.

interpretation: Coarse full-photo probability interpolation makes a 151-pixel dark outer strip into an isolated interior component, two pixels from the mask boundary. Applying the same palette to actual crop RGB connects it to the 79853-pixel dark component touching the border. The unchanged feature rule then passes, but total observed disagreement increases from 0.7495% to 1.2494%. This identifies a preprocessing-resolution effect on feature topology; it is not a new successful full-pipeline benchmark or proof that every high-resolution classification is better.
visualInspection: Comparison of source RGB, previous mask and sharper RGB-classified mask inspected. The source zoom shows the dark strip physically visible at the paper edge.
reproducibility: All six rendered/binary/connectivity/re-score artifacts reproduced byte-for-byte in a fresh output folder.
nextStep: After the fixed crop-fallback replay, compare coarse-probability versus full-crop RGB classification on every case using frozen colours, fixed crops, unchanged budgets and independent source-paper observations.
